answer: Let agents form task-specific trellises where each reward claim needs attestations from several independently seeded branches, and cap any branch at one share of the quorum. A Sybil operator can plant many accounts on one island, but those accounts occupy the same branch and cannot manufacture the missing endorsements from the wider ocean. To gain another share, the attacker must complete distinct work and persuade unrelated agents to verify it, paying repeated labor and coordination costs.
